subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default policy should OpenClaw enforce for externally or plugin-registered recurring `agentTurn` cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: Current code still auto-enables these jobs and inherits agent defaults, but changing activation, model, provenance, or quota behavior affects security posture, existing schedules, plugin APIs, and operator upgrades.

options.title: Require explicit activation and model disclosure
options.body: Default new external/plugin recurring model-backed cron jobs to inactive until a user-visible activation flow confirms schedule, model, delivery, and expected call rate, with doctor/update diffs for upgrades.

options.title: Keep auto-enable with strict cost warnings
options.body: Preserve enabled-by-default behavior but require explicit per-job model or visible cost warning/confirmation before recurring model-backed jobs can run.

options.title: Defer to narrower guardrail issues
options.body: Keep this issue open as product tracking while #14376, #42475, #71712, and #64721 settle the separate retry, budget, provenance, and schema surfaces.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation and model disclosure
recommendation.body: Default new external/plugin recurring model-backed cron jobs to inactive until a user-visible activation flow confirms schedule, model, delivery, and expected call rate, with doctor/update diffs for upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the original cron scheduler/default behavior and current plugin scheduling boundaries where steipete has the strongest history signal.
